result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers turn down the hero stat and the bigger cards for the right reasons, keep every truck the same size, and limit the summary to a thin strip of status counts. B does better on scannability: it keeps one fixed field order across every row and uses fixed-width, right-aligned door and minutes columns. It also uses a single exception treatment (left bar, bold minutes, ▲) with a rule to keep loud rows under about 10%. A's tiles change their field order between status columns and use two warning levels, which makes vertical scanning a little weaker, though its sort-by-door choice keeps tiles from moving around. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers reject the hero stat and bigger cards, keep every truck visible in a compact, same-size layout, and turn the summary into a slim strip. A is more disciplined: it uses one column order on every row, right-aligns the fixed fields, gives all exceptions a single treatment and caps highlighted rows at about 10%. B argues more fully against the user's idea, but its field order changes from one status column to the next, and its two-line tiles at 36–40px make the layout harder to scan straight down.
